page_sections.heading: Santa Fe Island — Land Iguanas, Turquoise Water, and Towering Cacti
page_sections.subheading: Santa Fe is a small, uninhabited Galápagos island (~24 km²) southeast of Santa Cruz. It is the only home of the Santa Fe land iguana (Conolophus pallidus). Visitors come for giant Opuntia cacti, a large sea lion colony, and excellent lagoon snorkeling. Day trips depart from Santa Cruz in about 40 minutes.

page_sections.content:
DATA SNAPSHOT — Santa Fe Island

The Santa Fe Land Iguana — Found Nowhere Else

Santa Fe hosts one of the Galápagos's most exclusive animals. The Santa Fe land iguana (Conolophus pallidus) lives only on this island. No other island in the world supports this species.

It is larger and paler than the common Galápagos land iguana (Conolophus subcristatus). This paler colouring gives the species its Latin name: pallidus.

For decades, introduced goats damaged the island's vegetation. The Galápagos National Park Service (GNPS) eradicated goats from Santa Fe in 1971–1972. The iguana population has since recovered. The most recent systematic survey (2005) estimated approximately 5,016 individuals (range: 4,500–5,800).

The IUCN classifies Conolophus pallidus as Vulnerable. Its entire global range is a single 24 km² island.

page_sections.title: Key stat
page_sections.content:
Only island on Earth where Conolophus pallidus exists.

2005 population survey: ~5,016 Santa Fe land iguanas (IUCN / Gentile & Grant 2020). IUCN status: Vulnerable.

The Cactus Forest

Santa Fe's interior is dominated by Opuntia echios — the Galápagos prickly pear. These cacti form a remarkable open forest visible from the beach.

Opuntia echios grows tall in the Galápagos because tortoises and iguanas graze it from the base. Plants that grew taller survived longer and reproduced more. Over thousands of years, this produced a naturally elevated trunk.

Santa Fe land iguanas cannot climb. They wait beneath the plants for fallen pads, flowers, and fruit. They eat spines and all.

The co-evolution between Opuntia and Galápagos herbivores is a textbook example of plant-animal co-evolution.

page_sections.content:
Snorkeling the Lagoon

Barrington Bay offers some of the best snorkeling in the Galápagos. The lagoon is calm and sheltered. Water is typically clear with good visibility.

Sea lions are the highlight. They approach snorkelers directly and swim rings around visitors. Eagle rays glide beneath the surface. White-tip reef sharks rest on the sandy bottom. Reef fish are plentiful throughout.

Skill level: beginner-friendly. No strong currents in the bay. Equipment is provided on day-trip tours from Santa Cruz. All snorkeling is supervised by a licensed naturalist guide.

How to Visit

Santa Fe has no permanent settlement and no airport. All visits arrive by sea. The most practical option for land-based travellers is a day trip from Puerto Ayora, Santa Cruz. Santa Fe is also a popular stop on central Galápagos cruise itineraries.

Note: Santa Fe is not directly accessible from Baltra (North Seymour airport) without first reaching Puerto Ayora, Santa Cruz.

items.question: Is Santa Fe the same as Barrington Island?
items.answer: Yes. Santa Fe Island is also known as Barrington Island, named after British Admiral Samuel Barrington. Both names refer to the same island. The visitor site at Barrington Bay carries this older name.

items.question: Can I see land iguanas and marine iguanas on the same island?
items.answer: Yes. Santa Fe has both the endemic Santa Fe land iguana (Conolophus pallidus) and marine iguanas (Amblyrhynchus cristatus). This makes it one of the few islands where both iguana types are visible in a single visit.

items.question: How long does a visit take?
items.answer: A day trip from Puerto Ayora takes approximately eight hours in total. The boat journey is about 40 minutes each way. On-island time covers both trails and snorkeling in Barrington Bay.

items.question: Is Santa Fe on most cruise itineraries?
items.answer: Not automatically. Santa Fe appears on some central Galápagos itineraries but is not on every cruise. Check your specific itinerary before booking if this island is a priority for you.

items.question: What is the snorkeling like?
items.answer: Barrington Bay is calm, clear, and beginner-friendly. Sea lions, eagle rays, and reef fish are common sightings. White-tip reef sharks rest on the sandy bottom.
